seoTitle: How to Move a Ticket to Backlog in Jira
metaDescription: Move Jira tickets from an active sprint back to the backlog for reprioritizing, reorganizing, or saving work for a future sprint.
intro: Not every ticket belongs in the current sprint, and sometimes you need to send a task back to the backlog to reprioritize. This guide covers how to move a Jira ticket from an active sprint back into the backlog quickly.

steps.heading: Open the active sprint board
steps.body: Go to your project's active sprint board where the ticket you want to move currently sits.

steps.heading: Select the ticket to move
steps.body: Right-click or open the options menu on the ticket you want to send back to the backlog.

steps.heading: Move the issue to backlog
steps.body: Choose the option to remove the ticket from the current sprint, which returns it to the project's backlog.

steps.heading: Reprioritize in the backlog view
steps.body: Once in the backlog, reorder or reprioritize the ticket for a future sprint as needed.

faq.question: Will moving a ticket to backlog delete its progress or comments?
faq.answer: No, moving a ticket to the backlog only changes which sprint it belongs to — all history, comments, and data stay intact.

faq.question: What's the difference between backlog and active sprint?
faq.answer: The backlog holds unscheduled work waiting to be planned, while the active sprint contains tickets your team is currently committed to completing.

faq.question: Can I move multiple tickets to backlog at once?
faq.answer: Yes, most Jira boards let you select several tickets and move them to the backlog in a single action.

faq.question: Does moving a ticket affect sprint reports?
faq.answer: Yes, if removed before the sprint closes, the ticket won't count toward that sprint's completed work in reports.
